correctness.rationale: For a four-run circle, factors of length at most one period have at most five runs. The one-, three-, and five-run palindromes are enumerated disjointly, including the equality cases where duplicate central lengths collapse. Their sum gives the exact four-case formula. The floor and parity inequalities establish the universal three-halves bound and all equality cases; a composition sum counts all maximizing parameters. The two-run formula proves sharpness, and direct run classification of the known six-run construction gives exactly ten t minus two palindromes. Two independent definition-level enumerators agreed on 3,836 finite examples, and 1,502,486 positive parameter quadruples were checked symbolically. The proof, not the experiments, covers infinitely many lengths.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal bound of 5n/3 does not imply the stronger restricted bound of floor(3n/2), the exact four-run identity, or the equality cases. A witness showing large counts at six runs does not alone exclude all four-run words. Because the full paper could not be inspected, it might contain a stronger hidden lemma: that is a named residual risk rather than falsely asserted noncoverage.

value.rationale: The circular-palindrome maximum is a central natural invariant. The four-run case is the first genuinely alternating binary circular class after two runs, not an arbitrary fixed word or a small table. The all-length exact formula and complete extremizer classification give a sharp structural barrier: exceeding 3n/2 requires at least six runs, and a known six-run infinite family shows this run threshold is optimal. The result clarifies which low-run circles can contribute to the 2014 global extremal phenomenon and leaves the unrestricted problem untouched.
